text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu shuts four Palestinian Authority offices in capital.
- Palestinian President Arafat: US President Clinton will save peace.
- French Foreign Minister de Charette to take message to Syrian President Assad.
- State revenues fall six percent.
- Canadian firm buys 25 percent of Phoenicia.
- Anti-trust Authority okays Generali purchase of Migdal.
- Renewed tender for Hapoalim published.
- Siemens consortium wins $9 million Gaza Airport tender.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu to Egypt this morning, will say to President Mubarak: 'Israel will build in har Homa and continue to hand over land'.
- Israel to United States: use Security Council veto.
- Syria prepres Scud missile test launch.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu orders closure of Palestinian offices in Jerusalem.
- Arafat calls for United States to establish embassies for two states in Jerusalem.
- Twenty-nine Palestinians appeal to High Court over Har Homa land confiscations.
- Tomorrow government decides on extent of first additional West Bank redeployment; pullback said to take place in two days.
- Israel rejects Arafat's request to move his plane from Al-Arish in Egypt to Gaza airport.
- Generali delays Migdal purchase after demand for veto on managerial appointments.
- Estimate: 3.9 percent rise in money supply in February.
MAARIV
- Work at Har Homa will begin with first further redeployment. Heavy American pressure to widen pullback.
- Hizbollah armed with Stinger anti-aircraft missiles.
GLOBES
- Sharp rise in capital inflows to economy at start of 1997.
